title: Linear Homepage Teardown: Jan 2020 to Jun 2026
h1: How Linear rewrote its homepage over 6 years
metaTitle: Linear Homepage CRO Teardown — Jan 2020 to Jun 2026
description: A CRO teardown of Linear's homepage from Jan 2020 to Jun 2026 — what changed in headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation, and what SaaS teams can study from it.
excerpt: Linear's homepage didn't just get updated. The headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation all shifted in a consistent direction between Jan 2020 and Jun 2026. This teardown maps what changed, when, and what the patterns may suggest.
author: Wael Aouididi
authorBio: SaaS Growth Marketer and fractional growth lead. I help B2B SaaS founders diagnose landing page, CRO, positioning, and analytics leaks before scaling traffic.

analysisBlocks.label: Jan 2020 — original state
analysisBlocks.heading: The original: product-led messaging
annotations: H1 opens with: "The issue trackingtool you'll enjoy using" — direct product statement.
Visible section headings include: "The speed teams needBuilt to be lightning fast", "Less managing, more meaning", "Meet your command line".
Navigation includes: "Changelog", "Twitter", "About us", "We're hiring!" — product category framing.
Section headings later removed include: "The speed teams needBuilt to be lightning fast" and "Less managing, more meaning".

analysisBlocks.label: Jan 2023 — mid-transition
analysisBlocks.heading: Mid-period: signs of a structural shift
annotations: Visual similarity to the previous snapshot: 59.2% — one of the larger layout changes in the dataset.
H1 in this snapshot: "Linear is a better way to build products".
New section headings appearing: "Unlike any tool you’ve used before", "Issue trackingyou’ll enjoy using".
Changes across this period appear incremental rather than a single redesign event.

analysisBlocks.label: Jun 2026 — current state

annotations: H1 now reads: "The productdevelopmentsystem for teamsand agentsThe product developmentsystem for teams and agentsThe product development system for teams and agents" — updated value proposition.

New section headings include: "A new species of product tool.Purpose-built for modern teams with AI workflows at its core, Linear sets a new standard for planning and building products.", "Make product operations self-driving", "Define the product direction".
CTAs no longer present include: "Request Early Access", "About us", "We're hiring!".

lessonCards.title: Your H1 signals which buyer you are targeting
lessonCards.body: The headline changed from "The issue trackingtool you'll enjoy using" to "The productdevelopmentsystem for teamsand agentsThe product ...". The framing of your H1 is one of the clearest signals of which buyer you are targeting and what you expect them to do next.

lessonCards.title: Navigation is a positioning statement
lessonCards.body: Navigation items changed from "Changelog", "Twitter", "About us" to "Customers", "Pricing", "Now". The labels your navigation uses reveal what you think your visitor is trying to decide — and who that visitor is.

lessonCards.title: Section headings reveal what the team thinks buyers care about
lessonCards.body: 7 section headings were added and 10 removed between Jan 2020 and Jun 2026. New headings include "A new species of product tool.Purpose-built for modern teams with AI workflows at its core, Linear sets a new standard for planning and building products." and "Make product operations self-driving". Headings that disappeared include "The speed teams needBuilt to be lightning fast" and "Less managing, more meaning". The pattern of what gets added and removed is one of the clearest signals of how a team is re-prioritizing its value proposition.

lessonCards.title: Incremental changes compound into a brand shift
lessonCards.body: Across 9 snapshots spanning roughly 6 years, no single update here was a dramatic overhaul. The end state looks very different from the start because small, consistent changes in the same direction accumulate. This is worth studying if your own homepage has been drifting without a clear direction.
